title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (August 2026 data) — the repeat-sales price read this calendar has never carried, 9:00 a.m. ET
source: NEWS: press.spglobal.com, fetched direct 2026-09-08, whose 2026-08-25 release "S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Index Reports Annual Gain in June 2026" (HTTP 200, 90,693 bytes) states the publisher's own schedule rule verbatim: "Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET." The last Tuesday of October 2026 is 2026-10-27. Corroborated by the publisher's own realized cadence on its news-release archive (press.spglobal.com/index.php?s=2429&mode=list&keywords=Case-Shiller, HTTP 200, 82,810 bytes, same fetch): every one of the nine dated releases listed since 2025-11 fell on that month's last Tuesday — 2025-11-25, 2025-12-30, 2026-01-27, 2026-02-24, 2026-04-28, 2026-05-26, 2026-06-30, 2026-07-28, 2026-08-25. Filed `estimate`, not `confirmed`, on three honest counts. (1) The publisher's own forward index-announcement schedule could NOT be read from this runner: spglobal.com/spdji/en/index-announcements/ and the index's own indicator page both returned HTTP 403, recorded in the proposing ledger's probe-ref.blocked rather than silently substituted, so this date rests on a stated rule plus a realized cadence and not on a published forward date. (2) THE CADENCE HAS SLIPPED ONCE INSIDE THE SAMPLE, and it is stated rather than dressed up: there is NO release in March 2026, and the January-2026-data report published 2026-04-28 alongside the February-2026-data report — a roughly four-week slip that then returned to cadence. (3) This lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts also has no member for an index owner's own publication schedule — the same gap the sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21 and Russell entries record. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the pending-home-sales-2026-10-20 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08, D-42). THE GAP IT FILLS: this calendar already tracks six housing series — NAHB HMI, housing starts, existing/pending/new home sales, FHFA HPI and NAR metro home prices — and carries NO Case-Shiller entry at all, despite it being the repeat-sales price benchmark the other price series are read against. It is proposed from the pending-home-sales lane rather than a price lane because the sweep that found it was reading NAR's own October block, and 10-27 sits seven days after the 10-20 PHSI print and on the same date as the already-tracked fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27 — two repeat-sales price reads on one morning, which is itself the attribution hazard worth having on the calendar. NAME NOTE: the index was renamed from "S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller" to "S&P Cotality Case-Shiller" and the publisher's releases now use the latter; a search on the old name will miss it. Impact `low` and `symbols: []` on the same measured basis as every sibling housing entry: no house playbook in docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md is macro- or housing-keyed, no instrument attaches, and the pending-home-sales-2026-12-17 lane measured a housing print's own release hour indistinguishable from an ordinary hour on ITB (33.9% vs 35.3% of session range, p=0.79). AUGUST DATA, NOT SEPTEMBER: Case-Shiller reports a three-month moving average with a roughly two-month lag, so the 10-27 report covers June-August closings and — unlike the 10-20 PHSI it sits beside — contains NOTHING signed after the 2026-09-16 FOMC decision. An estimate widens caution; nothing here licenses an entry.
